frames.label: High-precision measurements can be achieved without precision-made instruments by leveraging basic geometric references

frames.label: Indicate the fence to be aligned with the chosen machine axis within about 0.001 inch

frames.label: Use squares and parallels referenced off the indicated fence to align a chosen feature of each part to the machine axes
frames.main_point: Use squares and parallels referenced off the indicated fence to align a chosen feature of each part to the machine axes. Referencing a fence known to be within about 0.001 inch to an axis yields accurate part alignment.
frames.source_quote: Now when you go to put parts on the work table, you can use squares and parallels, referenced off your fence which you know is whiten .001" alignment of a particular axis(square to the other), to accurately align whatever feature on the part your using as the parts reference.

frames.label: Creating a datum chain—machine axis to fence to part—ensures the part ends up accurately located relative to the mach...
frames.main_point: Creating a datum chain—machine axis to fence to part—ensures the part ends up accurately located relative to the machine’s travel. Accurate referencing at each step propagates alignment to the final setup.
frames.source_quote: Then your parts will be accurately located withe respect to the fence, which is accurately located with respect to the axis' of travel.
frames.subject: datum chain from axis to fence to part
frames.thread_title: System for aligning/truing objects to each other in a plane for CNC machine

frames.label: Make the fence from precision-ground stock such as tool steel sized appropriately and rigidly mounted to the table
frames.main_point: Make the fence from precision-ground stock such as tool steel sized appropriately and rigidly mounted to the table. Using precision-ground material provides a straight, accurate reference edge.
frames.source_quote: pretty much a piece of tool steel stock, or anything precision ground say, 1/4" x 1" wide x however long you can fit, mounted to the working table at one of its ends.

frames.label: Successful photogrammetry requires carefully controlled lighting and target prep: eliminate shadows and gloss, apply...
frames.main_point: Successful photogrammetry requires carefully controlled lighting and target prep: eliminate shadows and gloss, apply a high-contrast nonrepeating texture, and capture many images from sufficiently varied angles. These steps improve feature matching and reconstruction robustness.
frames.source_quote: Photogrammetry is possible with free software, but the lights and the target should be prepared properly. The surface cannot have any shadows nor glosses, it must have high contrast non-repeating texture and one must take tens of photos from different enough directions.

frames.label: Keep lightweight subjects absolutely still during photogrammetry and eliminate airflow that could move them
frames.main_point: Keep lightweight subjects absolutely still during photogrammetry and eliminate airflow that could move them. Set the camera to manual so focal length and aperture remain constant across shots, avoiding calibration changes that degrade reconstruction.
frames.source_quote: The paper propeller doesn't stand any wind during the session and the camera must be in manual mode to keep the focal length and aperture constant.

frames.label: Replicate the real mounting when measuring a propeller blade by fastening the hub to a planar backplate
frames.main_point: Replicate the real mounting when measuring a propeller blade by fastening the hub to a planar backplate. This ensures the captured shape reflects the actual constraints present in use.

frames.label: Metrology equipment is not inexpensive, but you may be able to make do with some form of DIY construction

frames.source_quote: As noted in the comments, metrology equipment is not inexpensive, but you may be able to make do with some form of DIY construction.
frames.subject: DIY metrology approach
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Build a rigid metal frame around the part and use elements of that frame as your datums
frames.main_point: Build a rigid metal frame around the part and use elements of that frame as your datums. Keep the structure square with precise 90-degree angles to establish reliable orthogonal reference axes.
frames.source_quote: Create a (metal) framework that encompasses the part you are measuring, and plan to use segments of the framework as reference points. It's important to ensure that the angles of the structure you create are precise and 90b0 angles are your friends.
frames.subject: DIY metrology frame with orthogonal references
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Using a frame-and-strip transfer method can increase measurement precision, particularly for spans longer than your m...
frames.main_point: Using a frame-and-strip transfer method can increase measurement precision, particularly for spans longer than your measuring tools can reach. The reference frame lets you break long dimensions into accurately measurable segments.
frames.source_quote: You can measure the distance more precisely in this manner, especially if the distance exceeds your tools.
frames.subject: extending measurement range via reference frame
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Use triangulation between three points and apply trigonometry to verify or cross-check measured distances
frames.main_point: Use triangulation between three points and apply trigonometry to verify or cross-check measured distances. Independent geometric checks help catch errors and validate feature locations.
frames.source_quote: You can measure three points and use the math of triangles, aka trigonometry, either right triangles or otherwise, to confirm these measurements as needed.
frames.subject: triangulation for measurement verification
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Avoid chaining measurements from feature to feature; instead, reference all measurements back to a common datum
frames.main_point: Avoid chaining measurements from feature to feature; instead, reference all measurements back to a common datum. This reduces cumulative error and improves positional accuracy.
frames.source_quote: It's bad form to base measuring from one feature to another and proper form to base measuring from a reference point. You may not have that luxury in your situation, but minimize it when possible.
frames.subject: reference-based measurement vs feature chaining
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Brace the measurement frame heavily to keep it square and stable
frames.main_point: Brace the measurement frame heavily to keep it square and stable. For 3D setups, build a rigid cube with defined reference points to maintain geometry during measurement.
frames.source_quote: Use plenty of bracing on your metrology frame, ensuring that it remains square and true. If your frame has to be fully three-dimensional, you should have a solidly braced cube with specific reference points from which to measure.
frames.subject: metrology frame rigidity and squareness
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Be prepared to spend more time building the measurement fixture than taking the measurements themselves; the upfront...
frames.main_point: Be prepared to spend more time building the measurement fixture than taking the measurements themselves; the upfront effort yields better accuracy and repeatability. The investment pays off across the project.
frames.source_quote: Sometimes, the work you perform to generate such a frame will exceed in hours the amount of time necessary to collect the measurements, but the approach will pay off in the long run.
frames.subject: investment in fixturing for measurement
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Some measurement tasks cannot be done adequately with hand tools; a coordinate measuring machine may be required
frames.main_point: Some measurement tasks cannot be done adequately with hand tools; a coordinate measuring machine may be required. Without a CMM in such cases, you may be unable to obtain usable measurements.
frames.source_quote: In some cases you are be SOL without a CMM.
frames.subject: need for CMM for certain measurements
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: When a feature is difficult to access or define with standard tools, fabricating a simple custom fixture or gauge can...
frames.main_point: When a feature is difficult to access or define with standard tools, fabricating a simple custom fixture or gauge can make the measurement possible. Purpose-made aids are often necessary to capture certain dimensions.
frames.source_quote: Sometimes specific trinkets need to be made just to enable the measurement of one particular feature.
frames.subject: custom measurement fixtures
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: A low-cost way to capture X/Y locations on an irregular, heavy part is to level the flange and use tapered plumb-bobs...
frames.main_point: A low-cost way to capture X/Y locations on an irregular, heavy part is to level the flange and use tapered plumb-bobs hung from a frame to project feature centers for measurement. This lets you read coordinates relative to a reference with minimal specialized equipment.
frames.source_quote: If I had to do it simply and cheaply I would consider leveling the main flange of the component to be measured and using tapered plumb-bobs suspended from a frame.
frames.subject: plumb-bob method for XY hole/shaft location
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Establish an accurate, right-angled reference frame for the X and Y axes; that’s the only element that must be precise
frames.main_point: Establish an accurate, right-angled reference frame for the X and Y axes; that’s the only element that must be precise. Other fixturing can be relatively loose because measurements are taken to the reference axes.
frames.source_quote: You'd need a right-angled reference frame from which to measure your X and Y coordinates but everything else can be a lay-on sloppy fit.
frames.subject: orthogonal reference frame for XY measurement
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: If the plumb-bob isn’t suspended through a fine, central hole or on very fine wire, it can rotate away from vertical,...
frames.main_point: If the plumb-bob isn’t suspended through a fine, central hole or on very fine wire, it can rotate away from vertical, leading to coordinate errors. Ensure central, low-friction suspension to keep the bob truly vertical.
frames.source_quote: The plumb-bobs would need a fine hole dead-centre for the suspension thread or very fine wire to make sure that they don't rotate off vertical.
frames.subject: plumb-bob suspension alignment
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: You can use a single good plumb-bob, moving it to each feature in turn; final accuracy is governed mainly by how prec...
frames.main_point: You can use a single good plumb-bob, moving it to each feature in turn; final accuracy is governed mainly by how precisely you measure the X and Y distances to the reference axes.
frames.source_quote: Thinking some more, there's really no need for more than one decent plumb-bob that can be moved around. The exercise now depends on how accurately you can measure the X and Y distances.
frames.subject: single plumb-bob reuse and measurement accuracy
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: Use very large calipers to directly measure widely spaced features and hole positions on large parts
frames.main_point: Use very large calipers to directly measure widely spaced features and hole positions on large parts. Affordable 1 m calipers are available if you don’t already have such a tool.
frames.source_quote: First I would get some very large calipers. I just looked briefly and you can get chinesium calipers up to 1meter long for a few hundred bucks.
frames.subject: use of very large calipers for long-span measurement
frames.thread_title: Mounting an electric motor to a transmission: how to measure

frames.label: For this application, non-contact distance sensors will not achieve the required precision and spatial resolution
frames.main_point: For this application, non-contact distance sensors will not achieve the required precision and spatial resolution. Expect to use a contact measurement approach to reach the target accuracy.

frames.subject: non-contact distance sensor precision/resolution limits

frames.label: Plunger indicators provide a more direct linear displacement reading, while lever (test) indicators are better for sc...
frames.main_point: Plunger indicators provide a more direct linear displacement reading, while lever (test) indicators are better for scanning across a surface with lighter contact force. Choose plunger types for point accuracy and lever types for smoother contour tracing.
frames.source_quote: The plunger types give a more direct reading of distance but the lever types are more suited for scanning (i.e. dragging) across a workpiece and the contact force is also lighter.
frames.subject: plunger vs lever indicators for surface measurement
frames.thread_title: Sensor to measure distance with high precision

frames.label: Using a lever-style indicator to measure linear displacement introduces cosine error because the lever’s rotary motio...
frames.main_point: Using a lever-style indicator to measure linear displacement introduces cosine error because the lever’s rotary motion is converted into a linear reading. This geometric effect produces a systematic measurement error unless compensated.
frames.source_quote: The disadvantage of the lever type here is the cosine error since you are using a rotating lever to measure a linear distance.
frames.subject: cosine error in lever indicators
frames.thread_title: Sensor to measure distance with high precision

frames.label: You can adapt a plunger indicator for computerized digital measurement by attaching an external digital sensor to the...
frames.main_point: You can adapt a plunger indicator for computerized digital measurement by attaching an external digital sensor to the top knob (opposite end of the stem). A drag-wire sensor is one example, useful if you can’t get an appropriate digital indicator.
frames.source_quote: A plunger indicator also has the potential option for you to rig up a digital measurement device to the knob at the top of the indicator which is the opposite end of the stem where the probe is mounted. That way you could more more easily adapt a computerized digital measurement even if you can't get an appropriate digital indicator. Something like a drag-wire sensor, for example.
frames.subject: adding external digital readout to plunger indicator
frames.thread_title: Sensor to measure distance with high precision

frames.label: Driving a plunger indicator via an added lever increases flexibility but introduces cosine error
frames.main_point: Driving a plunger indicator via an added lever increases flexibility but introduces cosine error. The lever mechanism causes angular-to-linear conversion that biases the measurement unless corrected.
frames.source_quote: This will introduce the potential for cosine error again though but give you more flexibility.
frames.subject: cosine error when adding lever to drive plunger indicator
frames.thread_title: Sensor to measure distance with high precision

frames.label: Lever-style test indicators are difficult to modify beyond their stock configuration

frames.label: Calipers are suitable for measuring feature diameters but are not well-suited to accurately determine center-to-cente...
frames.main_point: Calipers are suitable for measuring feature diameters but are not well-suited to accurately determine center-to-center offsets to tight tolerances. Establishing precise C‑C positions between small features and a shaft is comparatively difficult with calipers.
frames.source_quote: I can measure the diameter of the bumps easily enough with calipers, but trying to establish center-to-center offset from bumps to the pot shaft with a reasonably tight tolerance is harder.

frames.label: A machinist (steel) square is great for smaller applications like small component mating surfaces

frames.source_quote: I have determined the Encoder is faulty as when i rotate it clockwise by one turn it increments by 5mm but when I rotate it anti-clockwise by 1 turn it increments by 10mm (approximately). It also feels quite clunky when i rotate it.

frames.label: When selecting a replacement encoder, prioritize matching the counts per revolution
frames.main_point: When selecting a replacement encoder, prioritize matching the counts per revolution. Also verify the output signal voltage with the manufacturer, even if 5 V is likely.
frames.source_quote: How many counts/revolution does the encoder output is the main important characteristic to choose a replacement. Voltage of the output signals is probably 5 V but it does not hurt to ask to make sure.

frames.label: Obtain the encoder’s technical specification and use it to cross-shop among vendors

frames.source_quote: - The technical spec can help you shop around from other vendors. You can all sales people of different companies and ask them if they have something compatible to your spec sheet.

frames.label: If you feed degrees into sine/cosine functions that expect radians, the computed transform will be incorrect, produci...
frames.main_point: If you feed degrees into sine/cosine functions that expect radians, the computed transform will be incorrect, producing unexpected/odd values. Ensure angle units match the math library’s expected input units to get the correct kinematic results.
frames.source_quote: Turns out my sine/cosine functions take radiant as input rather than degrees. As expected, the resulting transform matrix has "nice" values. Since my implementation and the other tool, which I checked the results with, both use rad as input. Consequentially I assumed the math was correct, which was false and resulted in odd numbers.
